  \caption{\textbf{Patch-leaving behavior is consistent with a Bayesian formulation of the Marginal Value Theorem.}
    (\subref{fig:2-a}) MVT schematic. An optimal forager leaves a patch when the instantaneous local reward rate falls below the global average reward rate, which is set by travel time between patches and within-patch reward statistics.
    (\subref{fig:2-b}) Bayesian MVT model schematic. The agent maintains a separate posterior over reward probability $q$ for each odor-cued patch type, updated after each binary outcome via Bayes' rule with a forgetting parameter $\delta < 1$ that discounts prior beliefs within a patch. At each odor site, a sample $\tilde{q}$ is drawn from the current posterior; the agent leaves if the implied local reward rate falls below a running estimate of the global reward rate $\bar{R}$.
    (\subref{fig:2-c}) Three behavioral metrics at patch leaving in mice ($N=24$): reward probability at leaving did not differ across patch types, whereas the number of stops and rewards collected were higher in High patches. Lines connect individual animals.
    (\subref{fig:2-d}) Same metrics for Bayesian MVT model simulations, reproducing the pattern in (\subref{fig:2-c}).
    (\subref{fig:2-e},\subref{fig:2-f}) Probability of leaving as a function of consecutive reward omissions at patch entry, in mice (\subref{fig:2-e}) and model (\subref{fig:2-f}). Mice left the Low patch more readily than the High patch after the same number of failures, reflecting odor-cued prior expectations about patch quality.
    (\subref{fig:2-g},\subref{fig:2-h}) Change in $P(\text{reward})$ at leaving, relative to control, as a function of inter-patch travel distance, in mice (\subref{fig:2-g}) and model (\subref{fig:2-h}). Longer distances lower the effective global reward rate, reducing the leaving threshold.
    (\subref{fig:2-i},\subref{fig:2-j}) Same as (\subref{fig:2-g},\subref{fig:2-h}) for inter-patch wheel friction. Increased friction raises the effective travel cost, producing equivalent threshold shifts.
    (\subref{fig:2-k},\subref{fig:2-n}) Reward probability depletion curves for the higher (\subref{fig:2-k}) and lower (\subref{fig:2-n}) global reward rate conditions. Solid lines show manipulated patch types; dashed lines show control.
    (\subref{fig:2-l},\subref{fig:2-m}) Change in $P(\text{reward})$ at leaving and change in rewards collected under the higher global reward rate condition, in mice (\subref{fig:2-l}) and model (\subref{fig:2-m}). Both patch types shifted, including the unchanged control patch.
    (\subref{fig:2-o},\subref{fig:2-p}) Same as (\subref{fig:2-l},\subref{fig:2-m}) for the lower global reward rate condition.
    (\subref{fig:2-q}) TODO: describe panel Q.
    (\subref{fig:2-r}) TODO: describe panel R.
    Significance (paired $t$-tests across mice): ns, not significant; $^{*}p<0.05$, $^{**}p<0.01$, $^{***}p<0.001$.}
